answer: Each challenge binds its task, account commitment, and deadline to a future drand quicknet round; only after its threshold-BLS pulse is published can the verifier derive the unpredictable instance—harbor, quartz, or forge—and validate a response. This prevents advance solution caching and replay across sybil accounts. Commit–reveal and rate limits raise the cost of parallel retries, while beacon randomness alone does not prove unique identities.
